blocks.h2: When a McHenry Sewer Line Needs Repair
blocks.intro: Cleaning fixes a clog. These signs point to the pipe itself:

tiles.body: If the line was cleared and the basement drain backs up again within weeks, something in the pipe is catching debris.

tiles.h3: A Sunken or Soggy Path in the Yard
tiles.body: Soil settling or staying wet along the route from the house to the street often marks a leak or a break.

tiles.h3: Slow Drains in a Newer Home
tiles.body: In a house from the 1990s or 2000s, slow drains that don't respond to cleaning often mean a sag where the line settled.
Cracks, separated joints or a belly in the line are a repair conversation, not a cleaning one.

blocks.h2: How Sewer Lines Fail in McHenry
blocks.intro: The median McHenry home was built in 1988, and about 3 in 4 went up between 1970 and 2009. Most lines here aren't ancient, but they have their own weak points.

items.body: When a subdivision goes in, sewer trenches are backfilled and the soil keeps settling for years. If the pipe settles unevenly, a section can sag. Water and paper collect in the low spot and turn into repeat clogs.
Homes from the 1970s and 1980s often have older pipe materials with joints roots can get through. Trees planted when those blocks were built are now big enough to find them.

items.h3: High Groundwater Near the River and Lakes
items.body: Close to the Fox River and the Chain O'Lakes, the ground stays wet. Water can get into a cracked line and add to what the pipe has to carry during wet seasons.
Some of the older houses near downtown and the Riverwalk still have original clay or cast iron, where roots and corrosion are the usual story.

blocks.h2: How We Handle Sewer Repair in McHenry
blocks.intro: Every sewer repair from our West Elm Street office starts with video.

steps.body: From the cleanout to the main, recorded, with the distance to every problem on screen.
A single bad section gets a spot repair. A failing line gets lining or replacement, and we show you why.
You get a flat-rate price first.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: In McHenry, the camera also tells us how deep the line is and whether high groundwater will affect a dig. That decides the method before we quote.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Why would a sewer line sag in a newer McHenry home?
items.preview: Soil settles after construction, and the pipe settles with it.
items.answer: When a subdivision is built, trenches are backfilled and the soil settles for years afterward. If the bedding under the pipe settles unevenly, a section dips. The camera shows exactly where and how deep the low spot is.

items.q: Can a sagging sewer line be fixed without replacing the whole thing?
items.preview: Usually. A spot repair at the low section is often enough.
items.answer: Usually. If the rest of the line is sound, we dig only at the sag, re-bed the pipe and replace that section. A [camera inspection](/mchenry/video-camera-sewer-inspections) tells us how long the low section is.

items.q: Does high groundwater make sewer repair harder?
items.preview: It can. We plan the dig around it.
items.answer: It can. Near the river and lakes, a deep excavation may need dewatering. That's one reason we look closely at [trenchless options](/mchenry/trenchless-sewer-repair) first.

items.q: Is the sewer line from my house to the street my responsibility?
items.preview: Usually, up to the connection at the main.
items.answer: In most cases, the private line from your house to the public main is the homeowner's to maintain. If the camera shows the problem is at the main, we'll tell you.

items.q: How much does sewer repair cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the damage, depth and method. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera finds, how deep and long the bad section is, the method and what's on top of the line. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
